title: dataset-tree-search-index-v1
description: An OPTIONAL flat search index for @freva-org/dataset-tree. It is not the tree's data source: browsing data comes from a DatasetTreeSource, and this document only decides what a search covers. It exists so that a search over a lazily-listed object store can reach objects nobody has opened, without the component recursively listing a bucket because somebody typed a letter. Closed: an unrecognised property is an error, never a silent drop. Identifiers must be stable and unique within one document; the runtime parser enforces uniqueness, which JSON Schema alone cannot express. The package never generates, fetches or refreshes this file - a consumer produces it however it likes and owns its freshness.

schemaVersion.description: Format version. A consumer that does not recognise the value must refuse the document rather than guess.

generatedAt.description: ISO-8601 instant at which the generator ran. Shown to the reader, because an index is a snapshot of something that moves and a result is worth exactly as much as its age. Optional and never invented.

source.description: The location this index describes, e.g. an object-store endpoint. Text only; never linkified and never fetched.

complete.description: Whether this index claims to cover the WHOLE archive. Required, and required to be explicit: it decides whether the component tells the reader the search covers everything indexed or keeps a caveat. A generator that cannot honestly claim completeness says false.

entries.description: Every searchable thing, flat. Flat and not nested: this document is not a second copy of the catalog, it is the projection search reads. A .zarr store belongs here as ONE dataset entry, never as its thousands of chunk objects.

entry.description: One searchable thing. A deliberately narrow projection of a tree node: the three strings search matches on, the two facts a result row shows, and the breadcrumb. Anything else a node can carry is absent on purpose - an index is held in memory and scanned on every keystroke, so a field search does not use is weight with no reader.

id.description: Stable, unique within the document, and NOT derived from array position. The same identity space as a tree node's id, which is what lets a result be deduplicated against a node that is already loaded.

name.description: The name as it appears in the store. Matched, and shown as the result's identity.

title.description: A friendlier display name. Matched, and shown beside the name.

path.description: Full location. Matched - including segment-exactly - and shown as the result's location. Rendered as text; never resolved or fetched.

size.description: Bytes. Rendered in binary units on the result row.

modifiedAt.description: ISO-8601. Rendered as YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM UTC; an unparseable value is shown verbatim.

ancestors.description: Root-first breadcrumb context. NOT tree nodes: a result may name something whose branch has never been loaded, and an ancestor written as a full node would invite inserting it into the browsing tree as though it had been fetched.
